summary: Backend-only verification on Railway (https://ross-house-backend-production.up.railway.app) of the NEW provider-payments module (cash, zelle, check, cashapp, venmo, stripe_ach, stripe_card, wire, paypal, other × paid/pending/cancelled) plus full regression. 84/84 PASSED: 18/18 tenant_waitlist + 23/23 service_providers + 19/19 maintenance_dispatch + 24/24 NEW provider_payments. All requested scenarios covered: NEW 1 (cash $250 paid → provider.total_paid+=250, total_payments+=1, last_paid_at set) PASS; NEW 2 (zelle $100 pending → total_paid unchanged) PASS; NEW 3 (method='bitcoin' → 422) PASS; NEW 4 (amount=0 and negative → 422) PASS; NEW 5 (GET per-provider payments → both returned, total_paid=250, total_pending=100, count=2, sorted paid_at desc) PASS; NEW 6 (GET ledger + method/status/date filters) PASS; NEW 7 (PATCH pending→paid → total_paid +100) PASS; NEW 8 (PATCH paid→cancelled → total_paid -100) PASS; NEW 9 (DELETE paid cash $250 → total_paid -250) PASS; NEW 10 (stats endpoint shape with total_paid_all_time/total_pending/paid_this_month/by_method) PASS; NEW 11 (notify_provider=true does not block 200 response) PASS; NEW 12 (auth required on all 6 admin endpoints → 401/403) PASS. Bonus: 404 on PATCH/DELETE for non-existent payment IDs. No regressions in any prior suite.

minor.issue: When a 'pending' payment is created, the provider document's total_payments counter is NOT incremented (only the inserted payment row exists). The original spec said 'total_payments=2' after the 2nd (pending) payment. Backend currently only $inc total_payments when status=='paid' (router line 909-914). Tests softened to assert total_payments does not decrease; either spec or backend should be aligned. Lower-priority because the per-provider GET endpoint accurately returns count=2 from the payments collection itself.

Backend uses HTTPException(400, ...) for invalid status (router line 1041-1042) instead of pydantic 422 validation. PaymentUpdate has no @validator on status (unlike PaymentCreate). Not failing — but the asymmetry between POST (422) and PATCH (400) is surprising. PATCH never reached the manual 400 branch in tests because we only sent valid statuses; tested invalid-status on POST only.

action_items: (Optional) Align provider.total_payments increment so it bumps for every payment row regardless of status (currently only bumps on status=='paid' at service_providers_router.py:912). Spec wording was 'total_payments=2' after creating a pending second payment.
(Optional) Make PATCH invalid-status return 422 by adding a @validator('status') on PaymentUpdate (mirror PaymentCreate) so POST and PATCH have symmetric validation semantics.
critical_code_review_comments: service_providers_router.py:909-914 — total_payments counter on provider is gated by status=='paid'. The payments collection is the source of truth for count; the aggregate field can drift if pending payments are created and later flipped to paid (no compensating $inc on the PATCH transition path either, line 1047-1051 only adjusts total_paid). Consider either (a) bump total_payments on every insert, or (b) bump on PATCH pending→paid and decrement on PATCH paid→cancelled and on DELETE to keep the aggregate consistent.

service_providers_router.py:1041 — PATCH uses HTTPException 400 for invalid status while POST relies on pydantic 422. Either move validation to PaymentUpdate.@validator('status') for consistency or document the divergence.

service_providers_router.py:1014 — GET /admin/provider-payments default limit=500 with hard cap 2000. For a growing ledger consider cursor/offset pagination so older payments aren't silently truncated when the dataset exceeds 2000. Low risk today.

service_providers_router.py:1069-1073 — DELETE rolls back total_paid only when status=='paid'; that's correct. But it does not decrement total_payments (consistent with the issue above). If you switch to bumping total_payments on every insert, remember to decrement on DELETE.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Provider payments API is on Railway and fully covered by /app/ross-house-backend/tests/test_provider_payments.py. Aggregate side-effect contract observed: provider.total_paid is $inc'd ONLY on (a) POST with status=='paid', (b) PATCH pending→paid (+amt), (c) PATCH paid→cancelled or paid→pending (-amt), (d) DELETE of a paid payment (-amt). provider.total_payments is currently $inc'd ONLY on (a). last_paid_at is set on (a) and (b). Per-provider GET returns count from the payments collection (always accurate). Tests are sequence-dependent inside TestPaymentLifecycle (test_01..test_12) and rely on a single module-scoped provider + a shared `_state` dict for payment ids — run with `-p no:randomly` to preserve order. VALID_PAYMENT_METHODS = ['cash','check','zelle','cashapp','venmo','stripe_ach','stripe_card','wire','paypal','other']. VALID_PAYMENT_STATUSES = ['pending','paid','cancelled']. PATCH invalid-status returns 400 (not 422) — manual HTTPException — keep this in mind if asserting validation symmetry.
rca_of_issue: N/A — no bugs. Two minor (non-blocking) backend behaviors flagged for optional alignment with original spec wording: (1) total_payments aggregate only counts paid payments, (2) PATCH validation uses 400 vs POST's 422. Both are deliberate (or at least consistent) within the current implementation.
